title: "Code windows"
subtitle: "Window chrome on code blocks, in the style of the preset."
description: "How the embedded code-window tool decorates code blocks in each format and preset, and how to change it."
---

The embedded [code-window](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-code-window) tool draws a window around each code block, with three traffic lights and the file name in the title bar.

````markdown
```{.r filename="compare.R"}
if (x != y && y >= 0) {
  z <- x |> sqrt()
}
```
````

## Look per preset

In HTML, Reveal.js and Typst, the window has the style of the preset:

| Preset | Window |
| --- | --- |
| `gold` | A gilded edge along the top of the title bar. |
| `mono` | A 2 px ink rule on top, square corners, no side edges. |
| `quarto` | A 1 px line frame on the tint, with 6 px rounded corners and a title bar a step darker than the tint. |
| `terminal` | A 1 px line frame on the tint, with square corners and a title bar a step darker than the tint. |

: The code window of each preset in HTML, Reveal.js and Typst. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

In Typst, the window also takes the tint of the preset behind the code.

## Options

code-window reads its options under `extensions: code-window:`.

```yaml
extensions:
  code-window:
    auto-filename: false
```

To remove the window from one block, use `code-window-enabled="false"`:

````markdown
```{.yaml code-window-enabled="false"}
key: value
```
````

Read the code-window documentation for all its options.

## Ligatures

Code ligatures are off for all code, in every format.
`!=` shows as two characters, not as one glyph.
